claims.claim: An output-fingerprint pin catches a planted template edit that changes every generated file before those bytes ship.
An unrelated whitespace-only change to generator.py does not trip the output-fingerprint gate.
Every generated artifact carries provenance naming its registry_id and generator_version.
Hash-pinning generator.py source bytes is an acceptable pre-ship gate.
claims.scoped_restatement: Pin generate() output bytes (tree_sha256), not generator.py source bytes. Source-hash would have tripped the whitespace plant; the output pin did not.
claims.why_locus: No DESIGN rule pins generator.py bytes. The sentence is the noisy alternative the catalog negative control forbids: whitespace-only source edits would trip it.

claims.claim: ARC-0010 TAMPERED detection of generated files intercepts a malicious template edit before ship.
claims.scoped_restatement: TAMPERED catches hand-edits of outputs. Template edits that then regenerate are intercepted only by comparing generate() to a previously authorized pin.
claims.why_locus: DESIGN hand_edit_rule compares output bytes to regenerate() from the current generator. A poisoned template regenerates CLEAN against itself. That is a different gate.

intercepting_gate.why_not_source_hash: A sha256 of generator.py bytes trips on unrelated whitespace. The catalog negative control forbids that gate.

named_template_files.why: Render functions emit every generated byte. A malicious edit here is a supply-chain execution node, not a hand-edit of an output.
Schema changes can widen what generate() will serialize.

question: In a generated architecture the generator and its templates are a code-execution supply-chain node: specify who may modify them, how a malicious template edit would be detected BEFORE it ships (review scope, signing, hash pinning), and whether every generated artifact must carry provenance back to its registry entry plus the generator version that produced it.

reviewer.method: Checked that named template files exist, that the output-fingerprint gate was executed on a scratch clone (planted edit caught; whitespace silent; missing pin fail-closed), and that REFUTED claims name DESIGN vs SENTENCE. Agreement that generated-SSOT is 'secure' is out of scope.

second_reviewer.method: Checked who-may-modify (two identities, including Codex), that provenance registry_id+generator_version is required by the gate, and that generator.py byte-hash is rejected as the ship gate.

scenario.catching_architecture: A2 output-fingerprint pin gate (ARC-0013/gate.py) against pins/output-fingerprint.json, authorized by a2-security-reviewer and codex-cross-vendor
scenario.on_this_estate: Live generate() writes 10 files. Planted edit changed 10/10 and the pin tripped. Whitespace did not trip the pin. Missing pin fail-closed. DESIGN control-plane/A2 generator path is absent; the named template file is ARC-0010/generator.py.
procedure: 1. Copy ARC-0010 generator.py, registry.json, and registry.schema.json into a scratch directory (clone analogue; live tree untouched).
2. generate() the live registry; pin sha256 of every output plus tree_sha256; require authorized_by both reviewers.
3. Plant a semantic provenance() edit (generator_id suffix) that changes every generated file; run gate.py against the original pin.
4. On a second scratch copy, insert whitespace-only Python outside string literals; generate(); assert the output pin is silent while generator.py source hash would trip.
5. Delete the pin input; assert the gate fail-closes (pin-absent), not a vacuous pass.
6. Parse provenance on every live generated file and require registry_id and generator_version.
scenario.title: Planted template edit vs whitespace-only vs missing pin

signing.honest_limit: This tree has no org signing key. The pin digest plus the two authorized_by identities is the demonstrated authorization, not a production GPG/cosign deployment.

strongest_surviving_counterargument: The output-fingerprint pin is itself a high-value target: whoever can change pins/output-fingerprint.json can authorize a poisoned tree. Dual authorized_by identities (security-reviewer + Codex) are the review scope on this tree, not org GPG. DESIGN still names control-plane/A2 as the generator home; those files are absent, so the live node is ARC-0010/generator.py. Do not rebuild A2 into control-plane to make the pin look like the dossier (that is the ADV circle). Strongest surviving FOR: typed regenerate plus provenance still catch hand-edits of outputs; that remains true and is a different gate.

generated_outputs.rule: Nobody hand-edits generated files. Restore is regenerate.

generator_templates.rule: Two-person, cross-vendor review: Anthropic-side security-reviewer AND Codex. Either alone is insufficient. Re-pinning outputs is the same two identities.

output_pin.rule: Updating the pin authorizes a new golden tree. Same two reviewers.

registry_entries.rule: Typed registry edits are architect-owned. If they change generated bytes, the output-fingerprint gate trips until the pin is re-authorized.
